151: The ground holds up even the people who dig into it. In the same way, the best thing you can do is calmly put up with people who insult you and look down on you.
152: Always put up with the wrongs people do to you, even when they go too far. Forgetting those wrongs completely is even better.
153: The worst kind of being poor is having nothing to offer a guest. The greatest kind of strength is staying patient with foolish people.
154: If you never want to lose your good, steady character, you must value patience and live by it every day.
155: People think nothing of those who pay back every wrong. But they treasure those who stay patient, like gold kept safe and wrapped up.
156: Getting even brings happiness for just one day. Staying patient brings praise that lasts as long as the world lasts.
157: Even when others hurt you in ways you did not deserve, it is good to feel sorry for the pain their wrong will bring them, and not to do wrong back.
158: When proud people do you great wrongs because they think they are above you, beat them with your own goodness, which means your patience.
159: People who can calmly take the harsh words of those who go too far are as pure as those who have given up the world.
160: People who go without food to train themselves are great. But they come second to people who put up with the cruel words others say to them.
161: Make it a rule for how you live to have a heart with no jealousy in it.
162: If you can stop being jealous of anyone at all, no other good thing you could ever gain is equal to that.
163: Someone who is jealous when others do well, instead of being happy for them, is really saying they do not want goodness or success for themselves.
164: Wise people know the trouble that comes from doing wrong, so they will never do wrong because of jealousy.
165: For jealous people, jealousy alone is enough to ruin them. Even if their enemies fail to hurt them, their own jealousy will bring them down.
166: A person who is jealous when others receive gifts will be ruined, and their family with them, left with no clothes to wear and no food to eat.
167: The goddess of good luck turns away from the jealous person and points them out to her older sister, the goddess of bad luck.
168: Jealousy is a wicked thing like no other. It wipes out a person's riches and pushes them down a path that leads to burning suffering.
169: When a jealous person grows rich and a good, honest person falls into hard times, it is something strange that we should stop and think about.
170: No one has ever become great by being jealous, and no one free of jealousy has ever lost the good things they had.
171: If you stop being fair and long to take someone else's good things, that greed will ruin your family and bring blame on you, right away.
172: People who are ashamed to be unfair will never do shameful things just because they want the profit those things could bring.
173: People who want the other, lasting happiness will never do wrong just to grab a small pleasure that soon passes.
174: People who see clearly and have control over their senses will not long for what belongs to others, even when they think, “We are poor and have nothing.”
175: What good is a sharp and wide-ranging mind if its owner wants other people's things and acts foolishly toward anyone at all?
176: Even someone who wants to be kind and has stayed on the right path will be ruined if they start wanting others' riches and plotting evil ways to get them.
177: Do not wish for riches that come from wanting what belongs to others. When those riches finally bear fruit, the result is hardly ever good.
178: If you ask what keeps your riches from shrinking, the answer is this: do not want the things that are in someone else's hands.
179: The goddess of good fortune knows the worth of wise people who understand what is right and do not want others' things, and she finds her own way to them.
180: Wanting others' things without thinking about what will happen leads to ruin. The proud strength of not wanting them leads to victory.
181: A person may never speak about goodness and may do only wrong. Still, it is good if people can say, “At least they do not talk badly about others behind their backs.”
182: Saying bad things about someone behind their back and then giving them a fake smile to their face is worse than turning away from goodness and doing wrong.
183: It is better to die than to live by saying bad things behind people's backs and being fake to their faces. Dying gives the real gain that the teachings of goodness speak of.
184: You may even say hard, unkind things to a person's face. But never say words behind their back without thinking about the harm those words will do.
185: When someone talks badly about others behind their backs, that small-minded habit shows that their heart is not truly good, no matter how much they talk about goodness.
186: A person who spreads other people's faults will have their own faults searched out, and the worst ones will be chosen and told about them.
187: People who do not know how to make friends through warm, friendly talk will say things that split people apart, even their own close friends.
188: If people make a habit of telling everyone the faults of those closest to them, what will they not do to strangers?
189: The earth still carries the person who waits until someone is gone and then says mean things about them. Is that only because the earth cares about being good?
190: If people could see their own faults the way they see the faults of others, could any harm ever come to anyone?
191: A person who keeps talking about useless things until many listeners are fed up will be looked down on by everyone.
192: Talking about pointless things in front of many people is worse than being unkind to your own friends.
193: When a person goes on and on about useless things, their talk itself shows everyone that they are not a good person.
194: Useless, rude words spoken in front of many people pull a person away from goodness and take away the good in them.
195: If even good people speak empty, useless words, they lose both their good name and the respect it earned them.
196: Do not call someone who loves to show off with empty words a real person. Call them the useless husk among people.
197: Good people may say things that are not pleasant if they must. But it is good for them never to say things that are useless.
198: Wise people who look for rare and valuable benefits never say words that do not bring great benefit.
199: People who see clearly, with no confusion or fault in their thinking, will not speak meaningless words, not even by mistake.
200: Of all the words you could say, say only the useful ones. Never say the ones that are useless.
201: People used to doing wrong are not afraid of the proud, careless feeling that wrongdoing brings. Truly good people are afraid of it.
202: Bad deeds lead to more bad things, so we should fear bad deeds even more than we fear fire.
203: Wise people say the highest wisdom of all is not doing bad things even to those who hurt us.
204: Do not plan someone else's ruin, not even without thinking. If you do, goodness itself will plan the ruin of the one who planned it.
205: Do not do bad things because you are poor. If you do, you will only end up even poorer.
206: If you do not want pain and trouble to hurt you, never do bad things to others.
207: People can escape even the worst enemies. But the enemy made by their own bad deeds never goes away. It follows them and destroys them.
208: Ruin stays with people who do bad things, just as a person's shadow never leaves them and stays right at their feet.
209: If you truly love yourself, do not go near any bad deed at all, even a small one.
210: Know this: a person who never steps off the right path to do wrong will be safe from ruin.
211: Real helping does not expect anything back. What does the world ever give back to the rain cloud that waters it?
212: All the money a person earns through hard work is meant for one thing: helping people who deserve help.
213: Neither in the world of the gods nor here on earth is it easy to find anything as good as helping others.
214: Only a person who knows how to help others in the right way is truly alive. Anyone else, though still breathing, counts as dead.
215: The riches of a wise person who loves to help the world are like a village pond filled to the top, there for everyone to use.
216: When riches come to a kind, generous person, it is like a fruit tree ripening in the middle of the village, where everyone can pick its fruit.
217: When riches belong to a truly good person, they are like a healing tree that always works, with every part of it used as medicine for others.
218: People who clearly understand their duty do not stop helping others, even when they themselves have less than before.
219: For a kind person, being poor means only one thing: the pain of not being able to do the good things they always do.
220: If helping others leads to ruin, that ruin is worth having, even if you had to sell yourself to get it.
221: Only giving to people who have nothing is true giving. Every other gift is like a trade that expects something back.
222: Even if someone says taking from others is a good way, taking is still bad. And even if giving did not get you into heaven, giving would still be good.
223: Not saying the sad words “I have nothing,” and giving anyway, is found only in a person of truly good family and character.
224: Being asked for help is painful for a giving person, but only until they see the face of the one who asked light up with joy.
225: People who train themselves by going hungry are strong. But they are less strong than people who take away the hunger of others.
226: Feeding the poor whose hunger is crushing them is the best place for a person with money to store it.
227: The burning sickness called hunger will hardly ever touch someone who makes a habit of sharing their food.
228: People with hard hearts hoard their things only to lose them in the end. Do they not know the joy of giving and being glad about it?
229: Eating alone, without sharing, just to keep your shelves full is surely worse than begging.
230: Nothing is more painful than dying. But even dying feels sweet when a person can no longer give to others.
231: Give to people in need, and live so that people speak well of you. There is no other real gain a person can get from life.
232: All the praise that people speak comes to rest on those who give something to people who ask for help.
233: In this world, nothing lasts forever except a great good name, which has no equal.
234: If someone earns a good name that spreads across the earth and lasts, the world of the gods will honor that person even more than its own wise beings.
235: A loss that is really a gain, and a death that lets you live on in people's memory, are hard for anyone except the truly wise to achieve.
236: If you are born into the world, be born with the qualities that earn a good name. If you do not have them, it would be better not to be born.
237: People who do not live in a way that earns a good name should be upset with themselves. Why are they upset with the people who look down on them?
238: Wise people say that for anyone on earth, it is a shame not to leave behind a good name.
239: When the land carries the body of a person with no good name, its rich, healthy harvest will grow smaller.
240: People who live without blame are the ones who truly live. People who live without a good name are not really living at all.
241: Kindness is the richest of all riches. Money and things can be found even in the hands of the worst people.
242: Think things through the right way and make kindness your rule for living. However many ways you test it, kindness is the one thing that truly helps you.
243: People whose hearts are full of kindness will never enter the dark world of suffering.
244: Wise people say that those who protect all living things and live with kindness will never have to fear what their own actions bring back to them.
245: Sorrow never comes to people who live with kindness. This big, windy, crowded earth is the proof.
246: Wise people say that those who give up kindness and live by doing wrong have lost sight of life's real purpose and forgotten the pain they once suffered.
247: This world has nothing for people without money, and the next world has nothing for people without kindness.
248: People who lose their money may do well again one day. But people who lose their kindness are truly poor, and they almost never get it back.
249: If you look closely, the good deeds of an unkind person are like a confused person claiming to understand the deepest truth. They are not real.
250: When you go to bully someone weaker than you, remember how you yourself felt standing scared before someone stronger than you.
251: How can someone who eats another creature's flesh just to grow their own body ever be truly kind?
252: People who do not take care of their money cannot enjoy having it. In the same way, people who eat meat cannot enjoy the gift of kindness.
253: Like the heart of someone holding a weapon, the mind of someone who enjoys eating another creature's body does not turn toward goodness.
254: If you ask what kindness is and what it is not: not killing is kindness, and killing is not. Eating the flesh of what was killed is wrong.
255: Life is kept safe by not eating meat. If a person eats meat, a place of terrible suffering will swallow them and never let them out.
256: If the world did not kill animals to eat them, no one would kill animals and sell their meat for money.
257: If people understood that meat is really the wound of another living creature, they would stop eating it.
258: People who see clearly, free of confusion and fault, will not eat the flesh of a body that has lost its life.
259: Not killing a single creature to eat it is better than making a thousand offerings by pouring butter into a holy fire.
260: All living creatures will put their hands together and honor the one who does not kill and refuses to eat meat.
261: Patiently bearing the pain that comes to you, and never hurting any other living thing: this is what true penance (a life of strict self-control) really is.
262: Penance (a life of strict self-control) works only for those who truly have its inner strength. For others, just going through the motions of it is useless.
263: Is it because others wanted to give food and help to the people who gave up the world that they forgot to practice self-control themselves?
264: If a person who practices strict self-control wishes it, that power alone can defeat enemies and lift up friends.
265: Strict self-control lets a person get whatever they want, just as they want it. So it should be worked at with effort, here and now.
266: People who practice strict self-control are doing their own true work. Everyone else is caught in the trap of wanting things and only works toward their own harm.
267: Gold shines brighter the more it is heated in fire. In the same way, people who practice self-control shine brighter the more suffering burns them.
268: A person who has fully let go of thinking about “me” and “my life” is honored by every other living being in the world.
269: For people who have gained the power that comes from strict self-control, even getting past death itself becomes possible.
270: So many people in the world have nothing because only a few practice strict self-control, and most do not.
271: When someone with a lying mind pretends to live a holy life, the five elements that make up their own body laugh at them from inside.
272: What good is looking as holy as the sky is high, if your own heart is full of wrongs that you yourself know about?
273: Someone with no control over themselves who dresses up like a strict holy person is like a cow eating crops while wearing a tiger's skin.
274: Hiding behind a holy look while doing wrong is like a hunter hiding behind a bush to trap birds.
275: People who say, “We have given up all wanting,” but live falsely will face many troubles that make them cry, “What have we done! What have we done!”
276: No one is more hard-hearted than people who have not truly given up the world in their hearts, yet trick others by acting as if they have.
277: Some people are bright red on the outside like the kundri seed (a small red seed), but inside they are as black as the seed's dark tip.
278: Many people with dirty minds bathe in holy waters as if they were great people, and they hide behind that show.
279: An arrow is straight but does harm. A lute (a stringed instrument) is bent but makes sweet music. So judge people by what they do, not by how they look.
280: There is no need to shave your head or to grow your hair long, if you simply give up what the world says is wrong.
281: If you never want to be looked down on, guard your heart so it never even plans to steal anything at all from anyone, even something small.
282: Even thinking in your mind, “I will trick them and take what they own,” is wrong.
283: Riches gained by cheating may seem to grow beyond measure, but they will be lost, and they will take more with them than they brought.
284: A deep habit of wanting to gain by cheating will, when it finally bears fruit, bring sorrow that never ends.
285: People who want others' things and wait for the moment someone is not paying attention cannot be loving people who care about kindness.
286: People with a hardened love for gaining by cheating cannot keep their actions within proper limits.
287: The dark cleverness called cheating is not found in those who have chosen the strength of knowing their limits.
288: Goodness stays firmly in the hearts of people who know their limits. In the same way, trickery stays firmly in the hearts of people who have learned to cheat.
289: People who know no way to live except cheating will be destroyed right in the middle of their wrong deeds.
290: For people who cheat, even their own life in the body will fail them. For people who never cheat, even the world of the gods will not fail them.
291: If you ask what truthfulness is, it is speaking words that cause no harm of any kind to anyone.
292: Even a lie can count as the truth if it brings about pure good with no harm in it.
293: Do not lie about what your own heart knows is true. Once you lie, your own heart will burn you with guilt.
294: A person who lives without lying, even inside their own heart, will have a place in the hearts of everyone in the world.
295: A person whose words are true and match their heart is greater than people who practice both strict self-control and giving to others.
296: No praise is as great as the praise for never lying. Without any extra effort, it brings every other good quality with it.
297: If you are truthful and never fail at it, that is enough, even if you do no other good deed.
298: Water makes a person clean on the outside. Being truthful shows that a person is clean on the inside.
299: Not every lamp is a real lamp. For wise people, the lamp of truthfulness is the only real lamp.
300: Of all the things we have found to be truly real, there is nothing at all that is better than truthfulness.
